why_it_is_not_an_n_plus_one: frontend/best_eta.go fans FindRoute out across drivers under a sync.WaitGroup: one call per driver is the work itself, not a per-row lookup, and the calls overlap. Their durations sum to more than the elapsed window, which is only possible if they ran concurrently.

grouping.note: The 11 siblings share the operation name HTTP GET but are not one group: one is a 1,309,571us customer lookup on :8081, the other ten are the route fan-out on :8083. Grouping by operation name alone, as step 2 says, lumps them together.

notes: This is the adversarial case: 11 identical sibling operations under one parent, which a count-only check flags as an N+1. Only the timing distinguishes it.

The answer is robust to how the group is drawn: both the all-11 and route-calls-only groupings give sum > window, so either reading reaches 'not an N+1'. Two models independently split off the customer lookup before measuring.
Concurrency is bounded — HotROD runs these through a small worker pool — so 8 of 10 adjacent pairs overlap rather than all of them. A rule requiring total overlap would also get this wrong.
Trimmed to the sibling group, its parent, and the ancestry to the trace root. 12 spans.
